claim: The note says らいねん breaks the せん／こん／らい pattern, but らいねん is built with らい〜 exactly like らいしゅう and らいげつ; only きょねん and ことし are irregular.
evidence: Card note: "きょねん (kyonen, 'last year'), ことし (kotoshi, 'this year'), and らいねん (rainen, 'next year') don't follow the regular せんげつ／こんげつ／らいげつ pattern". Book, WORD POWER time table: year row きょねん ことし らいねん beside らいしゅう, らいげつ. The deck's own chapter-6-extras/vocab-rainen-amerika-ni-ikimasu note says the opposite: "らいねん is the year-row 'next', matching らいしゅう for weeks and らいげつ for months." chapter-6/senshuu's note repeats the error ("but not the year words").
fix: Rewrite as: 'Last year and this year are irregular (きょねん, ことし) where the week and month rows use せん〜 and こん〜; next year, らいねん, keeps the regular らい〜.' and make senshuu's 'but not the year words' say 'only partly for years'.

claim: The へ card's hint glosses に as 'in/on/at', which the book has not taught and which contradicts the book's (and this unit's) gloss of に as 'to'.
evidence: Hint: "the alternative to に (ni, 'in/on/at')". Book, TARGET DIALOGUE vocabulary: "に to (particle; see GRAMMAR 2)"; GRAMMAR 2: "The role of the preposition 'to' in English is played by the particle に ... the particle へ ... can also be used in place of に." chapter-6/ni-particle: english "To (particle, indicates direction of movement)". No earlier card teaches に as in/on/at.
fix: Change the hint to 'the alternative to に (ni) for direction, pronounced e'.

claim: The AI sentence teaches ともだちたち, a redundant form most speakers and style guides avoid, when ともだち alone already reads as 'friends' and the book's own たち example is ひとたち.
evidence: Target: ともだちたちとこうえんにいきます 'I'm going to the park with (my) friends.'. chapter-6/tachi-suffix note also gives "e.g. ともだちたち (tomodachitachi, 'friends')", and chapter-6-extras/hitori-de-kouen-ni-ikimashita's note cites the same sentence. Book, SPEAKING PRACTICE: かいしゃの ひとたち, vocabulary "ひとたち people, 〜たち (plural for people)". ともだち (友達) already contains たち.
fix: Rebuild the example on a taught person noun that takes たち naturally, e.g. かいしゃのひとたちとこうえんにいきます, and use わたしたち or ひとたち in the tachi-suffix note; update the hitori-de-kouen note to match.

claim: The Production scene illustrates が with a だれが question, a pattern no card or book passage has taught; the book introduces が after どれ and どの.
evidence: Scene: "picking out which one of several, as in a だれが (dare ga, 'who …?') question". Book, SPEAKING PRACTICE NOTES: "The particle が ... is used instead of the topic marker は after interrogatives like どれ and どの." The card's own note uses only どの…/どれ examples.
fix: Change the scene to 'picking out which one of several, as in a どの… (dono, 'which …?') question'.

claim: The note says a bare はい would sound abrupt, but the book presents short はい／いいえ + verb answers as the normal reply and never says a bare はい is abrupt.
evidence: Card note: "Repeating ひとりで (hitori de) after はい (hai) is normal; a bare はい would sound abrupt." Book, GRAMMAR 1: "Answers to such questions can be brief, as in the examples below. ... はい、いきます。"
fix: Replace with: 'Short answers repeat the verb after はい; keeping ひとりで makes clear what you are confirming.'

claim: The note says a station name is 'never' joined to えき with の; とうきょうのえき is ordinary Japanese for 'a station in Tokyo', and the book says nothing about it.
evidence: Card note: "A station name glues straight onto えき (eki) with no の (no) between them — とうきょうえき (Tōkyō eki), never とうきょうのえき." Book, EXERCISES III vocabulary: "とうきょうえき Tokyo Station" only.
fix: Say: 'A station's name joins straight onto えき: とうきょうえき is Tokyo Station itself (とうきょうのえき would mean a station somewhere in Tokyo).'
